speaker: Doctor

I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present, and do they appear cyclically?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP; REQUEST TEST: Tzanck smear from blister fluid; REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of forearm lesions and oral ulcers.

text: RESULTS: CBC: Within normal limits; ESR: Not provided; CRP: Not provided; Tzanck smear: Not provided; Dermatology photos: Not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CBC and the specific combination of forearm blisters and oral ulcers, have you noticed if these lesions appear in cycles, triggered by stress or sunlight, or accompanied by eye pain or genital sores? This will help distinguish between conditions like Porphyria Cutanea Tarda, Pemphigus Vulgaris, or Behçet's disease.

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details. The pain during sexual intercourse and cheek pain alongside the blisters are concerning for genital and ocular involvement; can you confirm if you have experienced eye pain, redness, or vision changes? Additionally, have you noticed any skin fragility or blistering on your hands after minor trauma like touching glass or sun exposure?

REQUEST TEST: ANA, Anti-Centromere/Anti-Scl-70, and Direct Coombs Test.
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up of the oral ulcers and any new skin lesions.

text: RESULTS: ANA: Not provided; Anti-Centromere/Anti-Scl-70: Not provided; Direct Coombs Test: Not provided.

speaker: Doctor

With the recent start of captopril, could you confirm if the blisters appeared shortly after beginning this medication, and do you notice any new rashes on your face or neck? Also, have you had any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

REQUEST TEST: C3, C4, ANCA, and Direct Antiglobulin Test (Coombs); REQUEST IMAGES: Clear photos of the new forearm blisters and oral ulcers.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C3: Not provided; C4: Not provided; ANCA: Not provided; Direct Antiglobulin Test (Coombs): Not provided; Clear photos of the new forearm blisters and oral ulcers: Not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed that the blisters on your forearms become fragile and blister with minor bumps or sun exposure, and do the oral ulcers heal without scarring? Also, do you have a history of liver disease or have you recently been treated for gout?

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT) secondary to recent meloxicam use and possible hepatitis. The combination of blistering on sun-exposed areas (forearms), oral mucosal involvement, and a history of autoimmune disease (Graves', pernicious anemia) alongside the recent cessation of NSAIDs (meloxicam) and hypertension treatment points toward this diagnosis. Please ensure liver function tests are checked immediately and avoid further hepatotoxic drugs.
